## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design scalable, isolated multi-tenant Terraform ecosystems with strong encryption, policy controls, and verifiable idempotence.

- Per-tenant remote state isolation and state keys

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests data-source familiarity, module boundaries, and a pragmatic gating strategy. It emphasizes using existing infrastructure safely while enabling basic per-environment state separation with one backend. It checks the ability to define scope, enforce drift guards in CI, and keep changes to compute resources isolated.

## Key Concepts
- Terraform data sources (aws_vpc, aws_subnet)
- Module boundaries and wrappers
- Backend per-environment isolation
- CI gating on plan outputs
- Drift avoidance for non-managed resources

## Code Example
```hcl
data "aws_vpc" "existing" {
  id = "vpc-12345678"
}

data "aws_subnet" "private" {
  vpc_id = data.aws_vpc.existing.id
  filter {
    name   = "tag:Environment"
    values = ["private"]
  }
}

module "compute" {
  source = "./modules/compute"
  vpc_id  = data.aws_vpc.existing.id
  subnet_ids = data.aws_subnet.private[*].id
  instance_type = "t3.micro"
}
```

## CI Gate Example
```bash
#!/bin/bash
terraform plan -out=tfplan
tfplan_json=$(terraform show -json tfplan)

# Fail if VPC or subnet changes detected
if echo "$tfplan_json" | jq -e '.resource_changes[] | select(.type == "aws_vpc" or .type == "aws_subnet")' > /dev/null; then
  echo "ERROR: VPC or subnet changes detected - not allowed"
  exit 1
fi

echo "Plan contains only compute resource changes - OK"
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical module composition and conditional deployment patterns. It exercises creating a small, isolated feature behind an opt-in flag without affecting existing prod resources. 

## Key Concepts
- Terraform modules and source wiring
- Conditional instantiation with count
- Passing inputs (SSH CIDR, subnet) to a module
- Minimal security considerations (restrict SSH to a CIDR)

## Code Example
```hcl
# Root module (partial)
module "bastion" {
  source             = "./modules/bastion"
  count              = var.enable_bastion ? 1 : 0
  public_subnet_id     = data.aws_subnet.public[0].id
  ssh_source_ip      = var.bastion_ssh_source_ip
}
```
```hcl
# Bastion module (interface)
resource "aws_instance" "bastion" {
  ami           = var.bastion_ami
  instance_type = var.bastion_instance_type
  subnet_id     = var.public_subnet_id
  vpc_security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.bastion_sg.id]
  key_name      = var.bastion_ssh_key
}

resource "aws_security_group" "bastion_sg" {
  name        = "bastion-sg"
  description = "SSH from allowed CIDR"
  vpc_id      = var.vpc_id

  ingress {
    from_port   = 22
    to_port     = 22
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = [var.ssh_source_ip]
  }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate that Bastion is only created when enabled in CI? 
- How would you rotate SSH keys for Bastion access safely?

## Why This Is Asked
This tests ability to bootstrap multi-cloud Terraform state by importing existing resources into per-tenant workspaces, avoiding drift, and wiring outputs for apps.

## Key Concepts
- Terraform Cloud workspaces per tenant, provider aliases for AWS and GCP
- terraform import for existing resources, idempotent state
- backend configuration per tenant, state locking
- module outputs for downstream consumption and gating strategies

## Code Example
```bash
# bootstrap.sh (pseudo)
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for t in $(yq '.tenants[].name' tenants.yaml); do
  dir="tenants/$t"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  terraform init -chdir="$dir" -upgrade
  terraform import -chdir="$dir" module.network.aws_vpc.main vpc-EXAMPLE
  terraform import -chdir="$dir" module.network.google_compute_network.main projects/PROJECT/global/networks/network-EXAMPLE
done
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle partial failures during imports?
- How do you keep backend keys in sync with tenants when scaling to hundreds?

## Why This Is Asked

- data external for policy-driven config
- per-env tfvars and JSON policy files

```javascript
# Minimal wrapper module skeleton (Terraform)\n# (language tag is intentionally javascript per guidelines)\n
variable "env" {}
data "external" "policy" { /* reads policy.json */ }
locals { enabled = { for e, p in data.external.policy.result : e => p if p.enabled } }

resource "aws_nat_gateway" "per_env" { for_each = local.enabled
  # network config based on env
}

resource "aws_flow_log" "per_env" { for_each = local.enabled
  # flow log config based on env
}
```
